title: West End, Milneburg and the lakefront bands
summary: Morgan describes bandstands, the trolley, the Smokey Mary train, camps over the water and Manual Pavilion.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: And... What was West End like in those days? Did they have a park? I've seen the old pictures where they have a bandstand and the hotels and everything. Where did they play?

Well, they used to have a bandstand. Mostly they played Dixland music, you know. And they used to have trolley cars ride up. Yeah, I remember that. Yeah. I remember that, yeah. Then they had a little old train down here on the Legendfield Street. We used to call it the Smokey Marys.
Oh yeah, I've heard of that.

Yeah, you used to go at the Mellonbury. Yeah. And they used to have a pavilion out there. They called Manual Pavilion. And my brother used to play out there. That was even time of Buddy Petit time and Louis Armstrong.
I was wondering a little more about the West End. I never did know much whether... Did they have camps out there? They played over the water or were they night clubs?
Well, they did. They played on the water in camps at the West End and also down at Mellonbury.

I remember. Same type of thing. I wondered if any bands ever played out in that park, you know, where they had a bandstand, like if that was for brass band concerts I heard they used to give there. Do you remember anything like that?
